title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar
author: Eric Carle

hero.name: The Very Hungry Caterpillar
hero.description: Small green caterpillar with red head, distinctive Eric Carle collage art style
hero.source_note: Named/distinctive character in Eric Carle collage style — source from Creative Fabrica, TPT, or official Eric Carle licensed clip art

ambiguous.issue: Could mean 'full stomach / satiated' (feeling) or 'full container' (adjective for capacity)
ambiguous.reason: The caterpillar eats until his tummy aches — the meaning is 'satiated', not a container being full

ambiguous.issue: Could mean physically large (size adjective) or 'big deal / important' (abstract)
ambiguous.reason: The caterpillar grows big — physical size meaning is correct here

notes: Most key vocabulary (egg, cocoon, leaf, eat, hungry, full, butterfly, apple) already exists in activity_images or aac_extras — verify existing assets match Eric Carle art style for visual consistency. The book features many foods (pear, plum, strawberry, orange, watermelon, chocolate cake, ice cream, pickle, swiss cheese, salami, lollipop, cherry pie, sausage, cupcake, watermelon) but with only 11 fringe slots the priority is the life-cycle narrative words and the most iconic food. Apple is chosen as the single food representative since it is the first food eaten and most iconic. Days of the week (monday–sunday) are already in aac_extras and can be added to a supplementary page if the teacher wishes to extend the board. The transformation sequence egg → caterpillar → cocoon → butterfly is the core retell path and is fully covered by the chosen fringe.
